stories.title: Anthropic says single agents now beat multi-agent setups
stories.summary: Anthropic says companies should consider consolidating sub-agents into one agent that loads context on demand, since models can now handle more complexity alone. It published a migration kit on GitHub.
stories.more: In one architecture comparison Anthropic ran, a single-agent setup that loads context on demand ran about twice as fast as an equivalent multi-agent setup. Anthropic is recommending companies evaluate whether they can consolidate their sub-agents accordingly, and has published a migration kit on GitHub to help teams make the switch. It's unclear how general this speedup is across task types, or what tradeoffs in capability, if any, come with consolidation.

stories.title: OpenMobile-2 shows open smartphone agents can match proprietary ones
stories.summary: Researchers built OpenMobile-2, an open training environment with over 110 apps, and say the resulting smartphone agent scores highest among open agents on real Android devices.
stories.more: The researchers behind OpenMobile-2 argue that smartphone agents improve by training on a wide variety of different apps rather than simply processing more data. Their open training environment covers more than 110 applications, including 35 replicas of popular apps for safe training. On real Android devices, the resulting model scores highest among open agents, according to the authors. The excerpt doesn't say how it compares to proprietary smartphone agents, only to other open ones.

On real Android devices, their model scores highest among open agents, the authors say. stories.title: Jack Clark moves self-improving AI prediction up to 2027
stories.summary: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark now expects self-improving AI to arrive by 2027, citing a new benchmark from P-Zero Research that tracks how well models design and evaluate their own experiments.
stories.more: The P-Zero Research benchmark measures how capable AI models are at designing and evaluating experiments on their own, a proxy for self-directed research ability. Clark cited the benchmark's rapid improvement as the reason for moving his forecast forward. The excerpt does not specify the benchmark's methodology, scoring, or how much it has improved over what time period.

stories.title: OpenAI offers up to 90% discounts to poach Anthropic customers
stories.summary: OpenAI is undercutting Anthropic with steep price cuts, and customers including Rippling, Replit, and DataCamp say they've cut AI costs by up to 90% after switching.
stories.more: The named customers, Rippling, Replit, and DataCamp, say switching from Anthropic to OpenAI cut their AI costs by as much as 90 percent. The report frames this as OpenAI trading its own margins for market share while Anthropic's growth has slowed. It also notes that Chinese rivals such as DeepSeek are adding further price pressure on both companies. The excerpt doesn't give absolute dollar figures or say how many customers have switched in total.

stories.title: Schmidt and Ferguson cast OpenAI, Anthropic as AI-era trading companies
stories.summary: In Foreign Affairs, Eric Schmidt and historian Niall Ferguson argue the US and China are AI empires and other countries are dependencies, with the race decided by spending power rather than breakthroughs.
stories.more: The essay, co-written with researcher Lisa Klaassen, frames OpenAI and Anthropic as modern colonial trading companies extending US influence, and argues the AI race will be won by whichever superpower can bankroll it rather than by who finds the next breakthrough. It cites US corporations planning to spend more than $600 billion in 2026 on AI. The authors also point to risks that could stall both powers: mounting debt, growing protests against data centers, and a potential chip crisis tied to Taiwan. The piece does not specify a timeline for when the race might be decided.

stories.title: What the US anti-data-center movement can learn from abroad
stories.summary: Wired profiles Paris Marx, author of Hyperscale, on lessons the US data center opposition movement could draw from similar fights in countries like Ireland and New Zealand.
stories.more: The piece centers on Paris Marx, who has tracked global data center development for years and recently published a book, Hyperscale, on the subject. It argues the US movement against new data centers has much to learn from how similar opposition has played out abroad, citing Ireland and New Zealand as examples. The excerpt doesn't detail the specific lessons or policy outcomes from those countries.

stories.title: Nvidia open-sources Flora, a robot video labeling data engine
stories.summary: Nvidia released Flora, an open data engine that labels robot video far cheaper than GPT-6 Astra while scoring slightly higher on quality. It's built on three fine-tuned Qwen3.5 models.
stories.more: Flora labels one hour of robot video for 72 cents, versus $88 with GPT-6 Astra, according to Nvidia. The system is built on three fine-tuned Qwen3.5 models and catches errors in robot actions far more reliably than competing approaches, though it sometimes falls short on descriptive accuracy. Nvidia is positioning Flora as a key piece of its strategy to control the entire robotics value chain, from data labeling through deployment. It is unclear how the system performs on tasks outside the benchmarks Nvidia cited.
